groups.title: Basic syntax
groups.desc: From zero to writing small scripts – variables, containers, control flow, functions and objects.

groups.title: Advanced features
groups.desc: Magic methods, decorators, closures, async – understand Python's deeper machinery.

groups.title: Engineering & publishing
groups.desc: A modern project toolchain: pyproject + uv + ruff + pytest + publishing to PyPI.

python0: A starter before class begins – why Python is popular, what it can do, and whether it's worth learning.
python1: Meet Python and write your first line of code – this lesson runs in the browser, nothing to install.
python2: Start with print, then strings, numbers and variables – get Python talking.
python3: Ordered lists and unchangeable tuples – the two most-used container types.
python4: Key-value dictionaries plus duplicate-free sets – with List/Tuple they cover the whole data world.
python5: if / for / while, plus match/case, new in Python 3.10.
python6: Wrap up a piece of logic and reuse it – the foundation of every Python project.
python7: How for...in works, custom iterators, and generator functions with yield.
python8: Classes, inheritance, polymorphism – packaging data and behaviour together.
python9: import / from-import / a quick tour of the standard library – get your code organised.
python10: __str__ / __eq__ / __len__ / __add__ – make your own classes behave like built-in types.
python11: Replace magic constants with Enum, so constants explain themselves.
python12: Classes are objects too – make classes with three-argument type(), and control class creation with a metaclass.
python13: A quick tour of threading / multiprocessing: GIL, Lock, Queue, Pool.
python14: The re module: match, extract and replace complex patterns in text with one rule.
python15: A function inside a function that captures outer variables – understand closures and you understand decorators.
python16: One @decorator line adds logging, caching or permissions to a function – Python's most elegant syntax sugar.
python17: Good names + early returns + comprehensions + type hints – code others (and you, six months later) can read.
python18: Use Path objects instead of gluing os.path strings – clearer and harder to get wrong.
python19: try / except / finally / raise + custom exceptions – don't let one error crash the whole program.
python20: One decorator generates __init__/__repr__/__eq__ for you – goodbye boilerplate.
python21: What does with really do? __enter__/__exit__ + @contextmanager explained in one go.
python22: Coroutine basics: async def + await + asyncio.run + gather for concurrency.
python23: Modern Python project structure: standard pyproject.toml config + uv, the super-fast package manager.
python24: One tool replaces black + flake8 + isort + pyupgrade, 10–100× faster than the old combination.
python25: The industry standard: fixtures, parametrize, markers, coverage – tests can be elegant too.
python26: Upgrade print debugging to proper logs: 5 levels, format, getLogger, exception().
python27: From zero to pip install – src layout, uv build, uv publish: release a CLI tool of your own.
python28: All 29 chapters done – what next? Three paths: data/AI, web back end, automation.
